classification.difficultyReason: Use the earlier number as the percentage base, calculate relative change, and identify whether each result represents an increase or decrease.

content.prompt:
The number of shops in different shopping centres in Borrington changed from 2011 to 2012, but by quite different percentage amounts. Find the percentage increase or decrease in the number of shops where the numbers during 2011 and 2012, respectively, were:

Give answers to the nearest whole percent.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{New as \% of old}&=\frac{212}{200}\times100\%\\\text{New as \% of old}&=106\%\\\text{Percentage increase}&=106\%-100\%\\\text{Percentage increase}&=6\%\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\text{New as \% of old}&=\frac{160}{85}\times100\%\\\text{New as \% of old}&=\frac{3200}{17}\%\\\text{Percentage increase}&=\left(\frac{3200}{17}-100\right)\%\\\text{Percentage increase}&\approx88\%\end{align*}$$
To the nearest whole percent.

$$\begin{align*}\text{New as \% of old}&=\frac{122}{156}\times100\%\\\text{New as \% of old}&=\frac{3050}{39}\%\\\text{Percentage decrease}&=\left(100-\frac{3050}{39}\right)\%\\\text{Percentage decrease}&\approx22\%\end{align*}$$
To the nearest whole percent.

$$\begin{align*}\text{New as \% of old}&=\frac{110}{198}\times100\%\\\text{New as \% of old}&=\frac{500}{9}\%\\\text{Percentage decrease}&=\left(100-\frac{500}{9}\right)\%\\\text{Percentage decrease}&\approx44\%\end{align*}$$
To the nearest whole percent.
